correctness.rationale: The unitary twist makes log|w| globally defined and locally pluriharmonic. Add a strictly convex exhaustion of its interval to a strictly subharmonic base exhaustion; the base controls horizontal directions, the convex term controls vertical directions, and preimages with compact base and closed interior radial interval are compact. For the proposed base exhaustion, the punctured elliptic curve embeds as a smooth affine Weierstrass cubic by (℘,℘′). Laurent Parseval in the specified dw/w norm makes every coefficient locally L² at the puncture. Removability, unitary equivariance and Liouville force constants, with precisely the surviving degrees χ^k=1. Weighted square summability conversely gives local convergence by Cauchy–Schwarz with the convergent evaluation series. The area-one cell and Laurent norms C₀=2πlog 2, C_n=π(4^n−1)/n, C_{−n}=π(1−4^{−n})/n give the displayed formula, with the same factor on every term. Uniformly on compact interior radii, the ratio of the j≥2 tail to the leading pair is O(σ_I^{2q}) by summing geometric derivatives; the j=1 denominator contributes a smaller O(4^{−q}) relative error. For any approach to a character excluding that point itself, orders of the finite-order subsequence must tend to infinity, since bounded-order sets in this torus are finite. Thus the punctured limit is the baseline, giving the claimed jumps, continuity locus and upper semicontinuity.
residual_risks: Proof is for the specified intrinsic canonical norm, fixed unitary geometry and interior radii. The reported numerical comparisons are finite and are not a test of the global discontinuity statement.

originality.rationale: A distinct same-day Resultary source supplies the identical off-diagonal scalar series with the same Laurent norms, for a rational slice containing a character of every finite order; on its diagonal the target series is exact term for term. The stated sharp compact-interior jump size follows directly by taking the first pair and bounding the geometric tail of that series. The full two-torus is not literally the same domain of parameters, but the additional generator only adds the same scalar invariance condition on constant coefficients, replacing one order by a least common multiple; no new kernel calculation, analytical obstruction or rate results. The resulting global locus is the immediate finite-bounded-orders argument for this order-only profile. Hence no sufficiently distinct result is established after crediting the exact overlap and its consequences. This is a statement-level assessment, not an inference about priority from same-day dates or from an unread citation.
residual_risks: Same-day sources do not establish priority or independence. Reference [3] remains unresolved. The overlap is in the analytic mechanism and resulting order profile, not a claim that the rational-slice source literally states the full two-torus topology.

value.rationale: The exact Bergman density and its jumps are motivated invariants, but the meaningful quantitative content is already given by the known scalar profile and its first-pair expansion. The only residual extension imposes one more scalar period condition and replaces the rational parameter set by a rational grid; no new behavior of the kernel, quantitative regime or independent structural conclusion survives beyond the immediate order-only consequences. The record as a separate finding does not establish a worthwhile additional exact invariant or theorem.
residual_risks: The full torus description can still be useful exposition; this judgment concerns the marginal scientific contribution, not mathematical correctness or the usefulness of Bergman discontinuity examples generally.
